name: Telemetry
tagline: An OpenTelemetry receiver that joins your app's spans to the provider calls Stuntman answered.
point: UDP localhost:12201, or HTTP POST /gelf on :8025

capabilities.title: Traces, logs and metrics
capabilities.text: OTLP over HTTP (protobuf or JSON) and gRPC. GELF and StatsD land in the same logs and metrics.

capabilities.title: Spans meet provider calls
capabilities.text: Stuntman reads the trace ID on the way in, so a span to Azure Blob opens the call and the rule that answered it.

capabilities.title: Wait instead of sleeping
capabilities.text: wait_for_trace and wait_for_log return the first match after the agent acts in the app.

capabilities.title: Where the time went
capabilities.text: find_slow_spans lists spans over a threshold, provider spans first.

capabilities.title: Logs of one trace
capabilities.text: logs_of_trace gives every line the app wrote while serving a request; lines_around shows the context across services.

capabilities.title: Did the fix work?
capabilities.text: count_logs and compare_windows say whether an error stopped or a metric moved after a change.

capabilities.title: Why a metric jumped
capabilities.text: why_it_jumped finds the steps over twice the median and the breakdown value and Stuntman answer behind them.

capabilities.title: Calls that escaped
capabilities.text: real_provider_calls lists hosts the app still calls directly, from its own spans.

capabilities.title: Forward to a real APM
capabilities.text: Copy everything to a real backend; the API key is a Secrets reference, never a value.

excerpts.title: A trace joined to the provider calls

callouts.title: Touching a provider
callouts.text: Traces with spans that reached Stuntman, drawn in the provider's colour.

callouts.title: Provoked spans
callouts.text: Two Azure Blob PUTs answered 503 by a Stuntman rule.

callouts.title: The app gave up
callouts.text: No third attempt: the retry policy is visible in the span tree.

callouts.title: Answered by
callouts.text: The rule that answered the span, and a link to the object in Files.

callouts.title: Level and service
callouts.text: Counts per level and service; filter with list_logs or count_logs.

callouts.title: The error
callouts.text: The line the app wrote when the order failed.

callouts.title: Retries
callouts.text: Warnings for each 503 the app got, with the attempt number.

callouts.title: Trace id
callouts.text: Every line keeps the trace id the app sent, so it opens its trace.

callouts.title: Stuntman's side
callouts.text: Which rule made the uploads fail and why the app gave up.

callouts.title: Semantic names
callouts.text: Metrics grouped by provider calls, the app, runtime and custom.

callouts.title: Rule on
callouts.text: p95 jumps while a Stuntman rule was failing uploads.

callouts.title: 5xx
callouts.text: Errors the app answered while the rule was on.

callouts.title: Not Stuntman
callouts.text: A host the app still calls directly: a forgotten base URL.

callouts.title: Why it jumped
callouts.text: The step, the breakdown value that drove it and what Stuntman answered.

provoke.name: Refused
provoke.what: Connections to the collector are refused

provoke.name: Slow collector
provoke.what: Exports take longer: does the app block?

provoke.name: Half dropped
provoke.what: Half of the batches are dropped

provoke.name: Signal off
provoke.what: Traces, logs or metrics answered 200 and dropped

advantages.title: No APM bill
advantages.text: Traces, logs and metrics stay local per environment; nothing goes to a paid backend unless you turn forwarding on.

advantages.title: Cause and effect together
advantages.text: A span shows the provider call and the rule that failed it, which no real APM can see.

advantages.title: Built for agents
advantages.text: wait_for_trace, why_it_jumped and count_logs answer a question in one call instead of a dashboard.

advantages.title: Leaks become visible
advantages.text: Calls that bypass Stuntman show up from the app's own spans, so a test cannot quietly hit a real provider.

agent.prompt: After the order fails, find out why and whether the app really retried the upload.
steps: Azure Blob PUT × 2 · 503 · rule "Contract uploads fail twice" · no third attempt
tools: Traces by service, status, slowness or provider
The span tree with provider trips
Wait for the first matching trace
Spans over a threshold, provider spans first
Check an error stopped after a fix
Find what drove a metric jump

notes: UDP has no host name: GELF and StatsD go to the default environment, or the one a _stuntman_env field or stuntman_env tag names.
